verdict.rationale: LaunchDarkly documents its own automations that run unattended: scheduled flag changes fire at future points in time, and guarded rollouts raise traffic on their own while monitoring metrics for regressions. Its Autopilot marketing claims automatic shipping and rollback. These automations are limited to flag release workflows, and the scheduling covers one-off future changes or staged steps, not a recurring schedule. Missing for 10: general-purpose or user-defined background automations, recurring schedules, documented detail on Autopilot and adaptive triggers beyond titles or marketing, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Scheduling flag changes lets you define and schedule changes to your flag's targeting rules for future points in time.
A guarded rollout progressively increases traffic to the new variation while monitoring selected metrics for regressions until the rollout reaches 100%.
You can create a progressive delivery strategy by scheduling the incremental steps to release your feature to 100% of your user base.
Autopilot ships it safely, and rolls it back if it breaks.
